title: Sales Enablement: Unified Playbook - Positioning, Pricing, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Maya Thompson
summary: A consolidated sales enablement playbook covering positioning and messaging, competitive differentiation, pitch deck structure, pricing guidance, representative case studies, and a security FAQ tailored for prospect conversations.
body:
Introduction

Purpose: This playbook provides a single reference for Redwood Inference sellers and SEs to articulate our value, handle competitive situations, present pricing, and answer security questions during prospect conversations. Use the template slides, facts, and metrics below when preparing customer-facing material.

1. Positioning & Messaging

Elevator pitch (30s): Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform for running and optimizing LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. We deliver predictable latency, lower unit costs, and enterprise-grade controls so engineering teams can ship AI features without building inference infrastructure.

Top value props by persona:
- CTO/Platform: Unified runtime across environments (hosted/dedicated/private), capacity SLAs, observability and rollout controls.
- ML Engineer: Model versioning, quantization and batch tuning, KV/prefix caching, and integrated eval tooling for regression detection.
- Product Manager: Predictable unit economics, consistent user experience across regions, and built-in monitoring for quality and latency.
- Security/Compliance: VPC/private deployments, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logging, and SOC/ISO-ready controls.

Three core differentiators (how to say it):
1) Production-first performance: "We prioritize predictable throughput and latency - not just raw model access." Include benchmark data and latency SLOs.
2) Unified inference across environments: "Same API and rollouts whether hosted or on-prem - reduces engineering friction and risk." 
3) Cost-aware controls: "Batching, caching, and quantization recommendations tied to observed workload patterns deliver measurable unit-cost improvements."

Proof points & metrics to cite (always include source/date):
- Median p95 token latency improvements vs. unmanaged endpoints: 30-45% on typical chat workloads (Redwood benchmark, Q4 2025).
- Customer X reduced per-inference cost by 3.6x after quantization and KV caching (case study excerpt).
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for Dedicated customers; configured latency SLOs per-route.

Messaging dos & don'ts:
- Do: Emphasize operational risk reduction, measurable cost savings, and developer experience.
- Don't: Compete on model licensing or claim to be a model-training platform.

2. Competitive Briefs (short form)

Primary competitors: Major cloud AI endpoint services, LLM API providers, and self-hosted inference runtimes.

Competitive snapshots (talk track + defense):
- Cloud Managed Endpoints (A): Strength = integrated cloud infra; Weakness = limited workload-specific optimizations and opaque unit-costs. Defense: Show workload benchmarks and explain batching/caching levers.
- LLM API Provider (B): Strength = simple API and large model catalog; Weakness = less predictable latency, fewer private deployment options. Defense: Emphasize Dedicated and Private offerings and SLA-backed capacity.
- Self-hosted Runtime (C): Strength = control; Weakness = heavy ops burden, longer time-to-value. Defense: Position Redwood as hybrid alternative with turnkey private deployments and ops support.

Win themes: predictable economics, rollout/rollback controls, observability, and private deployment options.

3. Pitch Deck (recommended slide sequence)

Slide outline (title + key bullet for each):
1) Cover / One-line: Elevator pitch + logo
2) Problem: pain points (latency variability, high unit costs, brittle rollouts)
3) Solution: Redwood product overview (hosted, dedicated, private)
4) Architecture: high-level runtime + smart routing + caching
5) Differentiators: three core differentiators with metrics
6) Performance & Cost Benchmarks: p95 latency and $/1k tokens comparisons
7) Pricing Overview: tiers and guidance (short)
8) Case Study 1: Customer X (SaaS) - results highlighted
9) Case Study 2: Customer Y (Enterprise) - security and private deployment win
10) Roadmap & SLAs: Dedicated guarantees, private features
11) Next steps & ask: POC options, trial credits, SE support contact

Pitch tips:
- Lead with a customer problem and end with a clear next step (POC or pilot).
- Bring an SE for any live demo; avoid live model demos without an SE present.

4. Pricing Guidance

Pricing model: Usage-based for Hosted API (tokens/embeddings), committed monthly/annual pricing for Dedicated, and platform + support licensing for Private.

Standard public tiers (guidance):
- Developer (self-serve): $0.XX per 1k tokens, limited rate limits, trial credits for onboarding.
- Business (mid-market): volume discounts, per-model throughput guidance, access to Dedicated reservation options.
- Enterprise: custom committed capacity, private deployment pricing, premium SLAs and professional services.

Negotiation playbook & discounting guidance:
1) Anchor on measurable ROI (show expected $/1k tokens before/after optimizations).
2) Offer trial credits and a short-term pilot at reduced rates to validate performance and cost.
3) Use discounts tied to committed spend and multi-year contracts; escalate non-standard concessions to Sales Ops.

Recommended pricing table (example for negotiation conversations):
- Metric: Developer | Business | Enterprise
- Approx. $/1k tokens: $0.20 | $0.09-0.15 | Custom (0.05-0.12 after optimizations)
- Delivery: Hosted | Hosted/Dedicated | Dedicated/Private
- SLA: N/A | 99.5% | 99.9%+

Note: These numbers are guidance - always validate with Sales Ops for final quotes.

5. Case Studies (short abstracts)

Case Study - Customer X (SaaS analytics)
- Challenge: Latency spikes and high per-call cost during peak queries.
- Solution: Moved inference to Redwood Dedicated + KV caching and 8-bit quantization profile.
- Outcome: 3.6x reduction in per-inference cost, p95 latency reduced by 40%, seamless canary rollouts for models.
- Quote: "Redwood made it feasible to ship our AI feature without a months-long infra project." - Director of Engineering

Case Study - Customer Y (Financial services)
- Challenge: Compliance constraints and on-prem inference requirement.
- Solution: Private deployment with HSM-backed keys and audit logging enabled; strict network isolation.
- Outcome: Successful regulator review, production rollout at pilot scale, and ongoing dedicated support contract.

6. Security FAQ for Prospects (concise answers)

Q: Can Redwood run entirely in our VPC/on-prem?
A: Yes. We offer Private deployments with a customer-managed control plane and on-prem packaging for air-gapped environments.

Q: How are encryption keys managed?
A: We integrate with customer KMS solutions and support HSM-backed key storage for private deployments; hosted customers can use Redwood-managed KMS with customer-supplied keys in some plans.

Q: What audit logs and traceability are provided?
A: Request-level audit logs, API usage history, and per-route request tracing are available; export to SIEMs supported.

Q: Do you support SOC/ISO/GDPR controls?
A: Yes - Redwood maintains controls aligned to SOC 2 and ISO 27001; we provide GDPR data residency options and documentation for enterprise assessments.

Q: What is your incident response and notification policy?
A: Customers receive incident notifications per contractual SLAs; for Dedicated/Enterprise we provide post-incident reports and remediation timelines.

Salesplay quick pointers for security-sensitive prospects:
- Always offer a private deployment or dedicated capacity when SLAs or data residency are required.
- Prepare SOC/ISO evidence pack prior to deep procurement conversations.
- Loop in security engineering early for technical deep dives.
